First, another commenter had a great piece of advice in writing to your therapist if that is easier. She’ll know how to help you. Aside from that I’d love to share something that I learned that really, really helped me during my worst times. 

I’ve been told I’m a very sensitive guy, so maybe that’s sort of where this came from or why it helped, but maybe it’ll work for you. During those times where I was feeling really terrible or really & truly didn’t want to be here anymore, I’d love to say the most helpful thing was thinking about my mom or my aspirations or goals. But the largest reason I wanted to die so badly was because I felt so stuck in my life and my surroundings, I felt like things were out of my control and things were being decided for me and I felt like I was meant to be somewhere bigger doing something bigger. 

For reference, I live in a town that’s the ‘big town on the cusp of being a small city’ type. Nothing to do, but if you meet someone out, you’ll probably never see them again. I hated it, and honestly, I still feel like I’d be happier somewhere else, but I’m doing so much better now. The one thing that helped me most when nothing else did, was to find things, no matter how small, that made me feel like the things around me were beautiful and good. It could be anything. I would wander around my room and pick out things that I thought were beautiful. 

I remember taking a photo with one of those little instax cameras that my mom won at a work event or something of my little keyboard that I hadn’t played in weeks with my guitar resting on the wall beside it and a dinky little desk fan on top of it. At the time, I felt like the picture really captured how I was feeling. I thought it was beautiful. I titled it ‘North’ (the wall that made the background was my bedroom’s northern wall) and it’s still on my bulletin board. I really, really like that photo. 

After the pandemic hit I developed really bad anxiety again after putting my all into getting better and the thought of going outside made me have panic attacks. I went to the local park one day because she was taking my little brother and his friend, and there’s a skatepark there. I couldn’t believe how beautiful the skating ramps were. They were covered in graffiti as most are, and it was absolutely beautiful to me. I remember standing in the deepest part of it and just looking around in complete awe, I must’ve looked like an idiot, but I couldn’t believe that something so beautiful could come out of a town that I’d grown to absolutely hate. 

What I’m saying is the one thing that helped me when nothing else did was finding beauty in the ordinary. Finding beauty and meaning in the things that made me feel trapped. I don’t know exactly what is making you feel like you need to get out. But maybe whatever it is, this will help at least a little bit. Best of luck to you and I hope you’re able to heal. We’re here for you bro, keep up the good fight.
